top_sast_rules.description: An authorization check exists but evaluates access incorrectly.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-863 incorrect-authorization authorization-check permission-check role-check ownership-check acl-check access-decision bypass
top_sast_rules.remediation: Evaluate authorization from trusted server-side identity and policy state.

top_sast_rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-425 forced-browsing direct-request restricted-url protected-route protected-file missing-authorization route endpoint hidden-link
top_sast_rules.remediation: Authorize every protected route and resource on direct access.

top_sast_rules.description: An access-control policy is missing or incorrectly enforced for a protected resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-284 access-control authorization permission acl role owner ownership privilege protected-resource protected-endpoint allow deny
top_sast_rules.remediation: Require explicit server-side authorization before protected operations.

top_sast_rules.description: Use of a non-constant-time verification routine to check the value of an HTTP header, possibly allowing a timing attack to infer the header's expected value.

top_sast_rules.description: Legacy access-control category for failures in permissions, privileges, or authorization enforcement.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-264 permissions privileges access-control authorization acl role privilege owner permission enforcement
top_sast_rules.remediation: Enforce trusted authorization, role, ownership, and permission checks.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
top_sast_rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find code that may expose sensitive information in error messages, logs, or responses
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper access controls. Use generic error messages for users. Avoid exposing sensitive information in error responses, debugging output, or log files.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
top_sast_rules.description: Finds uses of symmetric cryptography algorithms that are weak, obsolete, or otherwise unaccepted. The key lengths allowed are 128, 192, and 256 bits. These are all the key lengths supported by AES, so any application of AES is considered acceptable.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Identify usage of weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithms and practices
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use modern cryptographic algorithms and proper key management. Avoid deprecated algorithms and implement proper random number generation.

top_sast_rules.description: Legacy category for failures in explicit software security features.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-254 security-feature authentication authorization confidentiality integrity cryptography privilege-management protection-mechanism
top_sast_rules.remediation: Apply the intended security feature consistently at the trusted boundary.

top_sast_rules.description: Disabling or weakening CSRF protection may make the application vulnerable to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attack.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find state-changing operations that lack CSRF protection mechanisms
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookie attributes and validate the Origin/Referer headers.
